name: Kairo
brief: Kairo turns a hunch into a trade. Type "I think SOL will be above $120 by Friday with $100" and Kairo prints you a ticket and places it on a fully onchain order book. Each contract pays $1 if you're right, the price is the probability, and you can never lose more than you put in. Live on Solana devnet with Pyth settlement, plus Base and Arbitrum. Crypto, stocks and real-world events.
what:
Kairo is options for people who don't want to learn options. You don't pick a strike chain or read greeks. You say what you think will happen, pick a level, a date and an amount, and Kairo prints a ticket you sign.

Under that simple surface is a real exchange. On Solana, each market is one account that holds a full central limit order book with price-time priority. Collateral sits in a program vault, and your YES or NO lands in your wallet as an SPL token. Every contract is fully collateralised (YES + NO = $1), so there's no margin and no liquidations. A maker prices every market from Pyth so the book is never empty, and if your strike or date doesn't exist yet, your first trade creates it in the same transaction.

It's for crypto-native people who already bet on direction with perps or on outcomes with prediction markets, and want something bounded, clear and onchain. It has a Serious mode for traders and an UwU mode for everyone else.
why:
Options are the right product sold through the wrong interface. People clearly want asymmetric, bounded bets: that's what prediction markets and lottery-style perps trades are. But option apps are built for market makers, and onchain options mostly live off-chain or in vaults.

The binary option is the simplest honest version: the price is the probability and the max loss is the premium. Solana is the first place where you can run the whole order book onchain, cheaply, one account per market, with Pyth publishing verified prices right next to it. No backend, no off-chain matcher.

We also noticed the next problem: liquidity is split across chains, and every chain has its own oracle and its own idea of "the price at expiry". So we wrote a paper, Canonical Events, on giving the same market the same key on every chain and settling it on the first oracle print after expiry. Kairo is the first step toward cross-chain options that don't need bridged collateral.
tech: Solana: Anchor 0.32 program with zero-copy market accounts (order book, maker seats, trade ring), PDAs, SPL Token for YES/NO and collateral, Pyth PriceUpdateV2 sponsored feeds on devnet, @solana/web3.js, LiteSVM and Rust fuzz tests. EVM venues: Solidity + Foundry (order book, quoter, maker vault), Chainlink feeds on Base and Arbitrum Sepolia, viem, an AggregatorV3-compatible keeper feed for 29 stocks, an optimistic resolver for event markets. Frontend: React 19, Vite, TypeScript, Vercel; original procedural night-sky and sakura art and hand-drawn chain-tan mascots in SVG. AI tools: Claude Code (Opus) orchestrating, OpenAI Codex (GPT-6.1) and Grok 4.6 through the Pi agent doing most of the implementation, a Claude Haiku manager coordinating them, and the models reviewing each other's security work.
chains_how: Solana devnet is home: our Anchor program (MonoTs1KRuamxFReiqsMzVt7gFM8bbn3QmEFjMbyazh) runs the onchain order book, vaults and SPL YES/NO tokens, creates markets permissionlessly inside the first trade, and settles on Pyth's first print at or after expiry. Base and Arbitrum Sepolia run the same product in Solidity with Chainlink settlement, stocks and event markets. The same market has the same key on every chain, and the app shows the best venue.
notes_who: No one outside the team. To be upfront: most of the code was written by AI coding agents working under my direction (Claude Code with Opus, OpenAI Codex, and Grok via the Pi agent, coordinated by a Claude Haiku manager), and the models reviewed each other's work. I made the product calls and checked everything by running it: 76 Rust and 61 LiteSVM tests on the Solana program, 366 Foundry tests on the EVM side, and real devnet and testnet trades.
notes_else: This is all testnet play money and nothing is audited. Try it at https://kairo-nu-red.vercel.app with Phantom or Solflare on devnet, or the built-in burner wallet plus "Get test funds". Known limitations are written down in the docs. Stock prices come from a keeper until we plug in a Pyth key. The paper is at /paper.
repo_context: Monorepo built during the hackathon. montions-sol/ is the Solana program, SDK and keeper (the core of this submission). montions-base/ is the EVM version for Base and Arbitrum. montions-app/ is the web app. paper/ has the Canonical Events paper, docs and thesis. The folder names still say Montions, the project's old name.
access: No login needed. Connect Phantom or Solflare set to devnet, or pick the built-in burner wallet, then press "Get test funds" for free tUSDC. Use the chain switch in the top bar to try Solana, Base or Arbitrum. Everything is testnet play money.
